title: The Metropole residency that built the 1960s band
summary: The Metropole paid salaries and let them come and go, a cramped place that quickly shaped the band; they place it in 1961-62.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So -- and I think what really put the '60s band -- I know what put it together, was the Metropolis. And the fact that it took a lot of responsibilities off of me. The salaries of the band and so on were paid by this place. And I was given actually a salary, that simply would take care of my immediate needs.
And we could pick and choose a time, if we got some good dates, we could go out for two weeks or four
weeks, and come back and go back in for two or four weeks, or whatever we wanted.
It was -- otherwise, I don't think that band could have been built at that time. I don't think there was that kind of interest or --

And it was a great place to break in a band, by sheer necessity, because you either played together or you'd never see each other again, being in a police lineup above a bar or playing into a mirror for a baffle.
That's right, yeah. But it really worked into a remarkable quick way to get a band in shape.
You had that Sea-Sack record in there, in December of '62, that band, and I was just wondering whether that was before.
No, that -- the Sea-Sack thing was done, actually, with another Allstar group, some of the guys, --
But, so, what you're talking about pre-dated --
